records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites and exclusively locks the entire posts table on this PostgreSQL-era stack, risking prolonged production downtime
records.rationale: The migration shown in the diff does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`, and on the PostgreSQL/Rails 3-4 era this stack is on (Gemfile_rails4.lock), adding a column with a non-null default rewrites the entire posts table under an exclusive lock. posts is the largest table in a Discourse install, so this is a concrete deployment risk grounded in the diff. It is not incorrect behavior (bug), but a substantive operational review concern a maintainer should act on (e.g., add without default then backfill, or use separate ALTERs).

This is a specific, diff-grounded test-coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic, not a product bug or a style nit.

records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:33 — The relative-URL example covers only root-relative paths, missing document-relative and protocol-relative href or src values that absolutize_urls currently leaves unresolved.
records.rationale: The finding is accurate and grounded: TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values with `href.start_with?('/')`, so document-relative links (e.g. 'images/wat.jpg') and protocol-relative URLs ('//host/img') pass through unresolved. The spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only exercises root-relative paths ('/hello', '/images/wat.jpg'), so the unhandled cases are untested. This is a specific missing-test/coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic, not a defect claim.
